body: ASSIGNED - and I only announced this on coordination, so if you have been reading narrative-visualization-vision you may not have seen it. That is my delivery gap, not your inattention. bd-01M16JJPDW36J3TWVBDJ5H6FFB, SLICE 2 (core), P1, yours. SEVEN types, CREDENCE FIRST: core/ids.scala:142. Its Scaladoc invariant - a calibrated value is present only if the calibration model that produced it is named - IS DESIGN-CONTRACT RULE 3, one of the thirteen non-negotiables, and fromProduct mints a calibrated probability with no named model in one line. Probability is an opaque type over Double with a public factory, so no payload protects it. Nine modules carry Credence. Then StorySource (core/atlas.scala:71), SpanSet (span.scala:71), TextSpan (span.scala:11), TokenRange (surface.scala:37), ClaimMeta (claim.scala:45), AudioSpan (transcript.scala:29). CORE IS THE FOUNDATION so your reference scope is the whole build - expect the widest gate of any slice, and it lands LAST of the three parallel slices for exactly that reason. READ docs/design/unforgeable-types.md FIRST (70 lines; criterion, three doors, and what does NOT close the door). Binding: fromProduct is the door; copy is ALSO live if the constructor is private[x] rather than bare private; the Product read surface only matters if the type hides a field. DEMONSTRATE THE FORGE BEFORE FIXING IT, and put a POSITIVE CONTROL beside every negative compile-time assertion - we have already had two that passed for the wrong reason. Your vision-topic contribution is welcome and is not a substitute for this; claim the bead and reserve your paths when you start.
